title: How is a ten digit number read in both systems?
description: A ten digit number gets its commas first, and is then read group by group in the Indian system and in the American system. Keeko then raises a hand, thinking the first digit sits in the crore place.
teaching_notes: One idea: place the commas first, and the group names tell the reading. Ask the class how many digits a number with a crore in front can have before any comma is placed. Watch for students who start the Indian reading at crore when the number has ten digits.

source: Read 9876501234 in the Indian system and in the American system
video_script.why: The child can place commas in both systems and knows lakh, crore and arab, and now reads a ten digit number in both.
video_script.substitution: Place the commas first, then say each group with its place name: arab, crore, lakh and thousand, or billion, million and thousand.
video_script.anchor: The ten digit number nine eight seven six five zero one two three four, with a row of Indian group names and a row of American group names.
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko starts the Indian reading at crore and says nine crore eighty seven lakh. A number with a crore at the front has only eight digits, but this number has ten, so its first digit is in the arab place.
video_script.payoff_line: The same number has two readings, one for each system

final_answer.value: Indian: 9 arab 87 crore 65 lakh 1 thousand 234. American: 9 billion 876 million 501 thousand 234
final_answer.spoken: nine arab eighty seven crore sixty five lakh one thousand two hundred thirty four in the Indian system, and nine billion eight hundred seventy six million five hundred one thousand two hundred thirty four in the American system

never_show: the comma written numbers before the answer beat
maths_rules: Indian groups from the right: 234, 01, 65, 87, 9 so 9,87,65,01,234
Indian reading: 9 arab 87 crore 65 lakh 1 thousand 234; 9 arab + 87 crore = 900 crore + 87 crore = 987 crore, so also 987 crore 65 lakh 1 thousand 234
American groups from the right: 234, 501, 876, 9 so 9,876,501,234
the slip: 9 crore is 9,00,00,000, which has only 8 digits, so a 10 digit number cannot begin in the crore place
video_script.design: One idea: place the commas first and read each group with its name. Wrong idea: Keeko starts the Indian reading at crore. The anchor stays all video; the working band builds in the idea part; no hard clear.
